issues.description: Dead code: NewRateLimit recreated then immediately overwritten — pointless allocation revealing confused logic
issues.detail: In the value_to_metric branch, the code calls NewRateLimit(...) to 'recreate' rateLimit, then immediately overwrites rateLimit.Stats with statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey). The first NewStats call inside NewRateLimit allocates a stats struct that is thrown away on the next line. This is exactly the kind of 'I didn't understand my own code' artifact that has no business landing. Delete the NewRateLimit call.

issues.description: Condition compares against rateLimit.FullKey which may never have been set, making behavior accidental
issues.detail: The guard `if enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` relies on FullKey being populated for the non-detailed_metric path. Looking at this diff, FullKey is only assigned in the DetailedMetric branch above. So for the common path, FullKey is empty string, enhancedKey is non-empty, and the override always fires. The 'optimization' is a no-op masquerading as a guard. Either always override or actually compare against the real existing stats key.

issues.description: Three nearly identical if/else branches that should collapse to one
issues.detail: The matchedViaWildcard / matchedUsingValue / default-key branches in GetLimit all do the same thing: write entry.Key, then if valueToMetric and entry.Value != "", append _value. This is textbook BAD-TASTE — three special cases for what is one rule. Collapse to: write entry.Key; if (valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue) and entry.Value != "" then append. The diff shrinks by 25 lines and the logic becomes legible.

issues.description: Two parallel metric-key builders traversing the same loop — wasted work for everyone who never enables the flag
issues.detail: Every GetLimit call now builds a valueToMetricFullKey strings.Builder regardless of whether any descriptor uses the flag. The detailed_metric path already does this same dance. For a hot path called on every rate-limit decision, paying this allocation+append cost when the feature is off is hostile to operators who don't use it. Track at config-load time whether any descriptor in the tree sets valueToMetric and skip the work when false.

issues.description: Struct literal positional initialization instead of named fields — bisect bait
issues.detail: `&rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}` adds a fourth positional field. Next person to add a field has to update every call site and risks silent field misassignment. Use named fields: `&rateLimitDescriptor{descriptors: ..., limit: ..., valueToMetric: ...}`. Costs nothing, prevents a real class of bug.

issues.description: Feature overlaps detailed_metric with no clear story for why both exist
issues.detail: detailed_metric already includes runtime values in metric keys. value_to_metric does the same thing but selectively per-descriptor. The README hand-waves about cardinality control, but a per-descriptor flag on detailed_metric would have solved the same problem without a second parallel codepath and a precedence rule. This is the kind of feature that grows a third flag in two years. Worth a maintainer conversation before landing, not after.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The feature is reasonable but the implementation has two real bugs and one taste problem. The NewRateLimit-then-immediately-overwrite-stats dance is dead code that reveals the author didn't fully understand their own control flow. The FullKey comparison guard is broken because FullKey isn't populated on the non-detailed-metric path, so the override always fires — accidental correctness. The three-way branch for building the enhanced key is textbook BAD-TASTE: three special cases doing the same thing. Fix those, collapse the branches, switch to named-field struct literals, and consider whether this should have been a per-descriptor flag on detailed_metric instead of a parallel feature. Then resubmit.
